result.topic_en: Euler turns a series of reciprocals with all positive terms into a continued fraction, then specialises to the series 1/ab − 1/bc + 1/cd − … and states Theorem II, which gives the corresponding continued fraction for 1/(as).

$\frac{1}{s} = m + \cfrac{mm}{n + \cfrac{(m+n)^2}{n + \cfrac{(m+2n)^2}{n + \text{etc.}}}}$
quem valorem iam XI Tom. Comentar. Vet. noſtrae Academiae dedi.

§. 21. Sin autem propoſita ſit iſta ſeries:
$s = \frac{1}{\alpha} + \frac{1}{\beta} + \frac{1}{\gamma} + \frac{1}{\delta} + \frac{1}{\epsilon} + \text{etc.}$
cuius omnes termini ſint poſitiui, tantum opus eſt vt in ſuperiore fractione continua loco litterarum $\beta, \delta, \zeta, \theta$, ſcribatur $-\beta, -\delta, -\zeta$, etc. tum igitur fiet
$\frac{1}{s} = \alpha + \cfrac{\alpha\alpha}{-\beta-\alpha+\cfrac{\beta\beta}{\gamma+\beta+\cfrac{\gamma\gamma}{-\delta-\gamma+\cfrac{\delta\delta}{\epsilon+\delta+\text{etc.}}}}}$
quae fractio facile transmutatur in hanc formam:
$\frac{1}{s} = \alpha - \cfrac{\alpha\alpha}{\alpha+\beta-\cfrac{\beta\beta}{\beta+\gamma-\cfrac{\gamma\gamma}{\gamma+\delta-\text{etc.}}}}$

§. 22. Pluribus autem modis ipſa ſeries propoſita transformari poteſt, vnde continuo aliae atque aliae fractiones continuae eliciuntur. Nonnullas igitur huiusmodi formas hic perpendamus. Sit ergo
$\alpha = ab,\ \beta = bc,\ \gamma = cd,\ \delta = de$ etc.

vt habeatur iſta ſeries:
$s = \frac{1}{ab} - \frac{1}{bc} + \frac{1}{cd} - \frac{1}{de} + \text{etc.}$
hincque formabitur iſta fractio continua:
$\frac{1}{s} = ab + \cfrac{aabb}{b(c-a)+\cfrac{bbcc}{c(d-b)+\cfrac{ccdd}{d(e-c)+\text{etc.}}}}$
quae facile reducitur ad formam ſequentem:
$\frac{1}{s} = ab + \cfrac{aab}{c-a+\cfrac{bc}{d-b+\cfrac{cd}{e-c+\text{etc.}}}}$
ſiue
$\frac{1}{as} = b + \cfrac{ab}{c-a+\cfrac{bc}{d-b+\text{etc.}}}$
quae forma nobis ſuppeditat ſequens theorema:

Theorema II.
§. 23. Si propoſita fuerit ſeries huius formae:
$s = \frac{1}{ab} - \frac{1}{bc} + \frac{1}{cd} - \frac{1}{de} + \frac{1}{ef} - \text{etc.}$
ex ea ſequens oritur fractio continua:
$\frac{1}{as} = b + \cfrac{ab}{c-a+\cfrac{bc}{d-b+\cfrac{cd}{e-c+\cfrac{de}{f-d+\text{etc.}}}}}$

Si propoſita fuerit ſeries huius formae:
$s = \frac{1}{ab} - \frac{1}{bc} + \frac{1}{cd} - \frac{1}{de} + \frac{1}{ef} - \text{etc.}$

items.english: Theorem II: If a series of the form s = 1/ab − 1/bc + 1/cd − 1/de + 1/ef − etc. is given, the following continued fraction arises from it: 1/(as) = b + ab/(c−a + bc/(d−b + cd/(e−c + de/(f−d + etc.)))).
